problem_text:
A retail distribution center must formulate a procurement and stock management strategy for a critical electronic component over a forthcoming 15-week operational window.  
The initial stockpile at the outset of the planning interval is precisely 69 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 15 \), the manufacturer permits the center to submit a procurement request whose size must fall within a range of 19 to 57 units.  
Nevertheless, every order submitted will incur a manufacturing and shipping delay of 3 weeks before it becomes available to fulfill requirements or augment the stockpile.  
The required quantity of the component in each week is provided as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 22 units  
* Week 2: requirement 20 units  
* Week 3: requirement 35 units  
* Week 4: requirement 13 units  
* Week 5: requirement 60 units  
* Week 6: requirement 59 units  
* Week 7: requirement 31 units  
* Week 8: requirement 58 units  
* Week 9: requirement 53 units  
* Week 10: requirement 43 units  
* Week 11: requirement 22 units  
* Week 12: requirement 56 units  
* Week 13: requirement 30 units  
* Week 14: requirement 21 units  
* Week 15: requirement 43 units  

Stockouts are permissible, but any unfilled requirement will be considered lost and not carried forward.  
Throughout the 15-week horizon, component quantities may be treated as continuous, and the aggregate quantity of physical stock on hand at any moment must not surpass the storage facility’s capacity of 69 units.  
The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three distinct elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 2 monetary units per unit ordered; the storage expense, amounting to 3 monetary units per unit of stock retained from one week to the next; and the penalty for unmet requirements, amounting to 15 monetary units per unit of unfilled demand. The objective is to ascertain the optimal procurement quantity for each week and to monitor the consequent stockpile and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
